answer: Weight follows the square of one lock. An identity locks 100 units for 10 epochs, scoring (100 x epochs) squared; splitting resets its clock. Each epoch, verifiers challenge the meadow staking plot, the walnut seal hashing that lock, and the oasis re-sign window, all at once in 10 minutes. A missed anchor, or one walnut hash serving two identities, zeroes the score. Splitting 100 units over 1,000 fakes gives each a score of 1, versus 1,000,000 intact, since squaring is per identity. A matching fake needs 100 units for all 10 epochs, 100,000 for 1,000 fakes, refunded after a clean exit check.
